intro: Short words from the Fathers of the Church on particular verses — Augustine, Jerome, Chrysostom, Ambrose, Gregory, Irenaeus, Origen and others — from public-domain translations, lightly modernised. Off by default; the text is the main voice. Turn them on in Reading options.

items.q: In the beginning, O God, you made heaven and earth in your Word, in your Son, in your Power, in your Wisdom, in your Truth — speaking in a wondrous way and making in a wondrous way.
The image is properly an image so long as it fails in none of those attributes which we perceive in the archetype. Man was made in the image of the One who rules over all: a royal creature.
The Lord recapitulated in himself that ancient enmity against the serpent... The knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary.
Isaac carrying the wood for the burnt offering is a figure, for Christ too carried his own cross. That Abraham says 'God will provide himself a lamb' is a prophecy: he knew the Lamb would come.
The angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man: ascending, when they are lifted up to contemplate his divinity; descending, when they come down to preach his humanity.
'I AM WHO AM.' This is the name of unchangeable being. Everything else, compared with him, is not — for he alone truly is.
O mystery new and inexpressible! The slaying of the sheep became the salvation of Israel, and the death of the sheep became the life of the people, and the blood turned back the angel.

items.work: On the Sermon on the Mount
items.q: The whole Law hangs on love. Whoever therefore loves God with all his heart cannot have a strange god beside him: there is no room.
He said not 'hear, O world', but 'hear, O Israel' — to those who had already seen his works. For the knowledge of God begins with remembering what he has done.
Jesus the son of Nun bears the name of Jesus my Lord; the book of Joshua does not so much tell of the deeds of the son of Nun as it depicts for us the mysteries of Jesus my Lord.
'Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth.' He who would be taught must first be silent. The soul that is always speaking never hears the Word that speaks in the heart.
David did not say 'this does not concern me'; he was not angry with the prophet; he did not remember that he was a king. He said: 'I have sinned' — and the sentence was at once suspended.
Job said 'the Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away' — and by this one word he wove himself a crown greater than all his patience before.
He asks Job where he was, that Job may learn where he is: a creature, questioned by his Creator, and answered by being questioned.

'Blessed is the man' — this is to be understood of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord-Man. He did not go in the counsel of the ungodly, as the first man did, who consented to his wife deceived by the serpent.
Why does Christ say 'why hast thou forsaken me' if not because we were there? The Head speaks in the voice of the body; he took on our words so that we might learn his.
'The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. In a place of pasture he has set me' — the pasture is the font, and the table prepared is the mystical table, and the cup that inebriates is his Blood.
Run to the fountain; long for the fountain of waters. Who is this deer? Whoever slays serpents — that is, sins — and then thirsts the more.
David, a king, fell; and a prophet came to him. He did not send the prophet away. This psalm is the king's confession sung every day in the Church, so that no sinner may despair.
'He that dwelleth in the aid of the Most High' — not he who visits, not he who passes through, but he who dwells. To dwell is to persevere.
The lamp is for the darkness of this life, the light for our path; but the day will come when we walk without a lamp, in the light of his face.
Out of the depths — Jonah cried from the belly of the whale, and was heard. Wherever you are, however deep, cry: he is deeper still.
'The Lord created me in the beginning of his ways' is said of the humanity the Wisdom of God took on for us, not of his Godhead; for the same Wisdom says, 'before the hills, I was brought forth'.

items.work: Commentary on the Song of Songs
items.q: This little book is an epithalamium, a wedding song, which Solomon wrote in the form of a drama and sang under the figure of the Bride about to wed the Bridegroom, the Word of God.

items.work: On the Incomprehensible Nature of God
items.q: The seraphim cover their faces with their wings — they cannot bear the sight. And we, who cannot see the seraphim, presume to search out the essence of God?
The word almah in Hebrew signifies not merely a young woman but a virgin kept in seclusion; and in this the Hebrews cannot contradict us, for it is never used of a married woman.

He was led as a sheep to the slaughter: of his own will, for he had said, 'I lay down my life, and no man taketh it from me.' The silence was not weakness but the silence of one who had already spoken everything.
'Before I formed thee in the womb I knew thee' — not that Jeremiah existed before he was born, but that God's knowledge does not wait on our beginning.

items.work: On the Spirit and the Letter
items.q: The law was written on tables of stone that man might be convicted of sin; the new law is written on the heart, so that what was commanded may be loved. That is the whole difference between the two Testaments.
The bones are the whole house of Israel in despair — and the whole of mankind in the tomb. Prophesy over them: the Word can put breath into what has been dead for a thousand years.
The fourth in the furnace, like the Son of God: he who would later descend into the fire of the world for us walked with them first, and the fire forgot its nature.
Jonah, our Lord's own figure, was three days in the whale; the Lord three days in the heart of the earth. Nothing in the prophet's story happens without meaning for the Church.

He begins with the genealogy so that you may learn that God became man in truth, born of a real family, with real sinners among his ancestors — Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, Bathsheba — for he came to take away sin, not to be ashamed of it.
Gold for the King, incense for God, myrrh for the man who would die: the Magi confess in their gifts what they could not yet say in words.

items.work: On the Sermon on the Mount
items.q: The poor in spirit are the humble and God-fearing, who do not puff themselves up. Rightly then does blessedness begin with humility — for the beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and pride is the beginning of all sin.

We say 'Our Father' and not 'my Father', because the Master of peace did not want prayer to be made singly and individually. Our prayer is public and common; when we pray, we pray for the whole people.
The word here for 'daily' is epiousion, which the Hebrew Gospel renders 'of tomorrow' — the bread of the age to come. We ask for the bread that is above all substances: Christ.
On this strength I will build an everlasting temple, and my Church, rising to heaven, shall be set upon the firmness of this faith.
Do you wish to honour the body of Christ? Do not neglect him when he is naked. Do not honour him here with silken garments while outside you leave him to suffer cold and nakedness.
Before the consecration it is bread; when the words of Christ have been added, it is the body of Christ. He said, and it was made; he commanded, and it was created.
The cry is not a complaint but a teaching: he who could not be forsaken shows how far he had come down to be with those who were.
Mark, the disciple and interpreter of Peter, handed down to us in writing what had been preached by Peter.
'I believe, Lord; help my unbelief.' Faith and unbelief in one man, one cry: that is every one of us, and it is enough for Christ to work with.
The centurion, a Gentile, confesses what the priests denied: the first fruits of the nations, gathered at the foot of the cross.

items.work: Homilies in Praise of the Virgin Mother
items.q: The angel awaits your answer, Mary; we too are waiting, we on whom the sentence of condemnation weighs. Answer, O Virgin, answer the angel; speak the word and receive the Word.
He who is enthroned above the cherubim has a manger for his throne; he who holds the world in his hand is wrapped in rags. It is my faith that he wanted the poverty.

A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho — Adam himself; Jerusalem, the heavenly city; Jericho, the moon, our mortality; the robbers, the devil and his angels; the Samaritan, our Lord; the inn, the Church; the two coins, the two commandments of love.
He ran to meet him while he was yet a great way off — for God comes to meet us before we arrive. He falls on his neck: it is the embrace of the Word made flesh.
The Eucharist is the flesh of our Saviour Jesus Christ, which suffered for our sins and which the Father in his goodness raised up.

items.work: Homily on the Cross and the Thief
items.q: The thief entered paradise before the apostles — not by works, for he had none, but by confession. Learn the power of a word spoken at the last hour.
They did not know him while he spoke, and knew him in the breaking of bread. Whoever wishes to understand what he has heard, let him hasten to do what he has heard.
I read there, not in these words but to the same effect, that in the beginning was the Word — but that the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us, I did not read there. That page is found only here.
He became man that we might be made God; he manifested himself in a body that we might receive an idea of the unseen Father.
'God so loved the world' — not the heavens, not the angels: the world, that is, men, ungrateful and sinning. And he gave, not a servant, not an angel, but his only Son.
Breaking one bread, which is the medicine of immortality, the antidote that we should not die but live for ever in Jesus Christ.
Why did Christ weep, but to teach us to weep? He who could raise the dead wept for the dead — and then raised him, that our tears too might end in joy.
He girded himself with a towel who clothes the heavens with clouds. Pride, be ashamed: God washes feet.
He is the way by which we go, the truth to which we go, the life in which we abide. Walk by the Man, and you arrive at God.
From his side flowed blood and water: baptism and the Eucharist. From these two the Church is born, as Eve from the side of the sleeping Adam.
The doubt of Thomas has done more for our faith than the faith of the other disciples; for as he touched, our minds are established beyond all doubt.
The Spirit came down upon the disciples so that all nations might enter into life; and so they gathered every tongue into unity, and offered to the Father the first fruits of all peoples.
'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?' The Head cries out for the members. He was in heaven, and he was being trodden on earth.
God judged it better to bring good out of evil than not to permit any evil to exist. Where sin abounded, grace did more abound.
All things work together for good — even their sins, for they rise from them more humble and more wise.

We do not receive these as common bread and common drink; but as Jesus Christ our Saviour was made flesh by the Word of God, so the food over which the prayer of his word has been said is the flesh and blood of that Jesus who was made flesh.
Faith and hope pass when we see; charity does not pass, but grows. What we love now by faith we shall love then by sight — and more.
O death, where is thy sting? O hell, where is thy victory? Christ is risen, and thou art overthrown. Christ is risen, and the demons are fallen. Christ is risen, and life reigns.
'I live, now not I' — the old man is dead; the new lives by another's life, and it is not less his own for being given.
The husband is the head, the wife the body: this is a great mystery, of Christ and the Church. Love your wife as Christ loved the Church — he did not threaten; he gave himself.
He emptied himself: not that he lost the Godhead, for he could not, but that he took what he was not — the form of a servant — and remained what he was.
The glory of God is a living man, and the life of man is the vision of God.
Faith is the substance of things hoped for: it gives the things that are not yet a body, and makes them stand before the mind as present.

Paul says a man is justified by faith without works; James says faith without works is dead. They are not at odds: Paul speaks of the works before faith, James of the works that faith must bring forth.
All who are reborn in Christ are made kings by the sign of the cross and consecrated priests by the anointing of the Spirit.

items.work: Homilies on the First Epistle of John
items.q: Love, and do what you will. If you keep silent, keep silent in love; if you cry out, cry out in love; if you correct, correct in love. Let the root of love be within, and from that root nothing but good can spring.
Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end: the beginning is Genesis, where the Word made all things; the end is here, where he makes all things new.
There we shall rest and see, see and love, love and praise. This is what shall be in the end without end. For what other end do we have, than to reach the kingdom that has no end?
